notCaptured.reason: No anchor chip exists in the reference page: a DOM query for 'a.chip, a.eg-chip, a[class*="chip"]' returned 0 matches, and the only link-mode traces are the Chip README 'href' prop and the 'a.eg-chip:hover' rule in bundle.css line 119. No real rendered link chip exists to capture, and no synthetic markup was rendered to fabricate one.

Covered by the approved v0.1 reference VIS-01 (docs/design/foundation-boards/v2026-10-17/Chip.png, sha256 a45c6772f1ab77e6d14cc45a05c518a17f3ae581e601b4e04884655c548c72ae); not re-captured because the v0.2 amendment does not change pressable appearance.

limits: The captures show the web's current local .chip/.topics styles, which are flatter than the design-system recipe (no sheen gradient, no edge shadow, 13/14px label). They are evidence for the role and content, not approved expected design for the Chip recipe.
pulso-source.html is a template with Jinja image placeholders and an external Google Fonts request; the chips do not depend on either, and the loaded font families are recorded above.
The reveal system starts every [data-reveal] node at opacity 0; the script forces the revealed state so the crop is not a pre-reveal capture. No source file is modified.
Static and interactive chips look identical except for pointer/keyboard affordances, so the captures cannot show mode by appearance; mode is a DOM and behavior property verified by tests.
The preview harness loaded Barlow 600 and Barlow Condensed 600 only, which covers the chip label weight (600); heavier weights used by other preview rows were not loaded.
Browser images do not verify behavior, accessibility, keyboard or focus behavior.

A localized difference in PNG bytes can appear between runs of the same script (scroll-dependent compositing); the hashes above are of the files stored in this folder and must be re-verified with sha256sum before linking them in any published comment.

approval.reference: Pending: the owner approves or declines these captures as supporting evidence for Chip v0.2 in issue #55. The captures are source evidence and grant no expected-design approval.
